clue.text: School stops ruffians thrashing poor kids

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so one piece sits inside the other as a stopper
thrashing suggests the ruffians are beaten about, so their letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A school puts an end to bullies beating up children from poor homes.
explanation.walkthrough: GAM, a school of whales, is the less familiar sense of 'School'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragamuffins are ragged, dirty children, typically from impoverished families.

clue.text: Work by 20 mainly a version of very hot 'Gremlins'

definitions.note: most of 20's answer is the author Roald Dahl, who wrote this collection of verse

indicators.note: a version is a reworking, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spicy adaptation of the film Gremlins credited to another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: '20 mainly' means most of the answer to 20, giving DAHL, Roald Dahl, author of this book of comic verse; The Gremlins was also his first book.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolting Rhymes is Roald Dahl's book of fairy tales retold in verse.

clue.text: Among Norwegian trolls he's big and friendly

indicators.note: among says the letters sit within the run of Norwegian trolls

explanation.surface: Among the trolls of Norway there is one kind, gentle fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition nods to Roald Dahl's BFG, the Big Friendly Giant, matching the Dahl theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahl's BFG is a big friendly being of enormous size, so a large gentle creature.

clue.text: Bird needing hormone replacement

indicators.note: replacement says the letters of hormone are put back in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A bird is in need of hormone replacement therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: The moorhen is a common water bird with a red bill.

clue.text: Women send documents over Irish Sea almost

indicators.note: the fax goes over the other pieces, covering them on either side

parts.note: to fax is to send documents by phone line

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so sea loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Women send documents across the Irish Sea, or nearly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish Sea' looks like one place; it gives IR and SE separately, wrapped in FAX.
explanation.definitionFit: The fair sex is a dated collective term for women.

clue.text: Rider, ordered to keep up tempo, burst in

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the rearranged letters hold the other pieces
ordered means arranged, so the letters of rider are put in a new order

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for tempo in music

explanation.surface: A jockey told to quicken the pace burst onto the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider, ordered' makes IRRED, which holds the tempo letters; 'up tempo' looks like one musical phrase but splits into UP and T.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to enter forcibly or suddenly, so irrupted means rushed in.

clue.text: Blair astonished injured hero from Baghdad

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, stunned and hurt, is cast as a hero from Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad is the seafaring adventurer of the Arabian Nights tales, set in Baghdad.

clue.text: Quiet game capturing hearts

indicators.note: capturing means taking in, so the game holds the other piece

parts.note: whist is a card game
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games

explanation.surface: A silent card game in which hearts are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisht is a Scottish and Irish exclamation meaning hush, be silent.

clue.text: Order Matilda initially to head off without one

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of Matilda
off means out of sorts, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without means lacking, so one letter is removed

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: Matilda is told to leave at once, alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without one' drops A from TOHEAD, and 'off' rearranges TOHED into ETHOD. Matilda is a Roald Dahl heroine, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a system or orderly way of doing things, so order in that sense.

clue.text: Try port shortly before

indicators.note: shortly says the word for port is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a haven is a harbour or port
ago means before now, in the past

explanation.surface: An instruction to sample some port, quickly, before something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try port' reads as wine-tasting advice; 'port' is the harbour, HAVEN, docked to HAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go is the idiom for making an attempt at something.

clue.text: Batting line-up attainable

parts.note: a side batting in cricket is said to be in
a range is a line or row of things, such as a mountain range

explanation.surface: A cricket batting order that looks within reach of victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Something within range can be reached, so the phrase means achievable.

clue.text: Spots plan during chess game

indicators.note: during places the plan in the middle of the chess letters, as something happening within them
game here means willing to play about, so the letters of chess are rearranged

parts.note: a plot is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: Someone notices a strategy being hatched in the middle of a chess match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' reads as describing chess, but it is the anagram signal, game meaning ready to be played with.
explanation.definitionFit: Splotches are blotches or irregular marks, a synonym for spots or stains.

clue.text: Low-priced fruit?

parts.note: a penny apiece is low-priced, and the question mark flags that the price tag, written P for penny then the word for apiece, spells the fruit

explanation.surface: A query about bargain produce at the greengrocer.
explanation.walkthrough: Priced at a penny each, written P EACH, is low-priced; with no word left over for a definition, the whole clue works as one cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A peach is a soft, downy stone fruit, and a penny apiece makes it cheap.

clue.text: Viz misses nothing to poke fun at

indicators.note: the phrase misses a letter, leaving it out, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: viz is short for videlicet, meaning to wit or namely
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: The comic magazine Viz loses nothing by mocking its targets.
explanation.walkthrough: Viz is also a British adult comic famous for crude satire, which is the surface picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To twit someone is to tease or taunt them, an older word for mocking.

clue.text: It's surprising you have to install Windows etc after crash

parts.note: U is text-speak for you

indicators.note: to install something is to put it inside a computer, so these letters go into another piece

parts.note: to have to do something is to need to
XP is a version of Microsoft Windows

indicators.note: after a crash the letters are left jumbled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek remark that a crashed PC needs Windows reinstalling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have to' as a phrase means need; here 'have' supplies it and 'to install' is the container signal. 'after crash' rearranges the Windows and etc letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexpected is not foreseen, which is what makes it surprising.

clue.text: Cool sister holds drugs party, slurring words?

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool

indicators.note: holds means keeps inside, so the sister contains another piece

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
E is short for ecstasy, a drug
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A trendy nun hosts a drug-fuelled party where speech gets slurred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slurring words' suggests drunken speech; it means words that cast slurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Innuendo is insinuating remarks that hint at something disparaging, so a slur by implication.

clue.text: Design study so no microphones appear

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, so
mics is short for microphones

explanation.surface: A design study has been conducted without any microphones present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' looks like a link word, but it is the Latin therefore, ERGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomics studies how to design workplaces and equipment around the people using them.

clue.text: Old river rises about noon, making sea warmer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the river goes round another piece
in a down clue rising means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: An ancient river swells around midday, heating up the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N into NILE to give NINLE; with O before it the whole ONINLE reads upwards under 'rises'.
explanation.definitionFit: El Niño is the periodic warming of Pacific surface waters off South America.

clue.text: Puzzle compiler's pen hides ruler

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, so compiler's is my

indicators.note: hides means conceals within, so the pen holds the ruler

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: The setter's pen conceals a measuring stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' and 'ruler' suggest stationery; they are a pigsty and the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystery is something baffling, an enigma or riddle.

clue.text: Children are being injected with £1 drug

indicators.note: being injected means having something put inside, so the word are holds another piece

parts.note: the pound sign is L, from libra, and 1 is I

explanation.surface: Kids are being given a drug that costs a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie is slang for cocaine.

clue.text: Went to the front, bypassing western offensive

indicators.note: to bypass is to go round, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to have led is to have gone in front

explanation.surface: Someone moved to the front, avoiding a rude western film.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd means crude and lascivious, so it is offensive to good taste.

clue.text: Trouble did upset occupant of bed

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
had can mean did, as in had a meal

explanation.surface: An illness turned someone upside down in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bed' suggests a sickbed; it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A dahlia is a garden flower grown in beds, so something that lives in one.

clue.text: Statesman in need, hard up now and then

indicators.note: now and then means occasionally, so only every other letter of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A politician, cash-strapped and needy, is sometimes short of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, a noted statesman.

clue.text: Scrawny tennis player makes funds available

parts.note: spare can mean lean or thin
Pat Cash is an Australian tennis player, Wimbledon champion in 1987

explanation.surface: A skinny tennis player is making money available.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare cash is money left over and free to be used.

clue.text: Join new part close to top

indicators.note: close means the final letter, and to top says it goes to the head of the word

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A newcomer joins in a role near the top.
explanation.walkthrough: NROLE has its last letter, E, moved to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up as a member, so to join.

clue.text: One ordered to guard this writer's candidate

indicators.note: to guard something is to surround and protect it, so the rearranged letters go round another piece
ordered means arranged, so the letters of one are put in a fresh order

parts.note: this writer is the setter, so this writer's is mine

explanation.surface: Someone is told to protect the setter's preferred candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One ordered' reads as a person given orders; it is the word one rearranged, wrapped round MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A nominee is someone put forward for a post or award, a candidate.

clue.text: Left two lots of foreign money for rock attraction

parts.note: ore is a coin of Scandinavian countries
lei is the plural of leu, the Romanian currency

explanation.surface: Leftover foreign currency is used for a rock music attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two lots of foreign money' supplies two currencies, ORE and LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a rock on the Rhine whose legendary siren lured boatmen to their deaths.

clue.text: Writer and salesman screening blue tales at first

indicators.note: to screen something is to shield it, so the salesman goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a seller is someone who sells
blue is the colour of the UK Conservatives, so a blue is a Tory

indicators.note: at first takes just the opening letter of tales

explanation.surface: A writer and a salesman are hiding smutty stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue tales' looks like rude stories; 'blue' is a Tory, from the British Conservative Party's colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A storyteller is a narrator or author of tales, a kind of writer.
